findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that there were four cans which we sharply dented along the upper/lower seams of the cans in the dry storage area and not separated or logged for discard prior to the inspection. PIC is aware that these cans must be discarded and always checks prior to using the cans that there are no dents, however, as cans are available for use in the facility, hazardous ones must be separated out and not stored with those which are not damaged to prevent accidental use. The dents were significant enough that the integrity of the can is in question. 

Operator immediately removed the cans and separated them out to be discarded. Corrected on site. Ensure that cans are checked prior to placement on the rolling shelf with the rest of the cans to prevent accidental use during operations. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A spray bottle was observed under the counter to the right of the dish machine area where the chemicals are stored which didn’t have a label. Operator believes that the bottle was used for bleach. However, without any label, operator did not appear certain of the contents of the bottle. Ensure that labels are placed on all containers in the facility when hazardous chemicals are taken from their original container. Bottle was removed from service during inspection. Corrected on site. 

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following areas throughout the facility were observed to be missing caulking or the caulk is deteriorating:
- Behind the basins of the triple sink where the caulk is subject to moisture, gaps are forming in the caulking and the caulking is becoming soft and pliable.
- The caulking behind the hand sink is missing and needs replaced.
- The caulking behind the dish sprayer to the left of the dish machine is missing/deteriorating and needs replaced.
- The caulking behind the double sink is missing/deteriorating and needs replaced.

Ensure that these areas are re-caulked before the next routine inspection. Ensure that caulking is monitored for deterioration and that these areas are maintained often enough to prevent deterioration. 

The laminate behind the double sink is peeling away from the lower portion of the back splash exposing bare wood in an area subject to moisture. Reattach or replace the laminate to keep this area smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

Inspector observed cabinet door handles along the lower wall towards the dining room. These door handles must be replaced to maintain the facility in good repair and allow operators to open doors without grabbing other parts of the cabinets to get them open. 

All physical facilities repairs/maintenance are to be corrected by next routine inspection.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
REPEAT> Observed the gauge on the heat booster to the dish machine to be reading between 163 during the rinse cycle even after multiple cycles. Manager ran a heat strip through, which changed color indicating that the dish is reaching 160F. Based on this, it appears that the sanitizing cycle is working correctly, however, the gauge is not reflecting this and is in need of repair. Repair gauge on heat booster to show that the water coming out at the manifold is 180F during the rinse (sanitizing) cycle.
750-830c A thermometer ±3°F shall be provided to check the temperature of  the water in each tank of the dish machine and the temperature of  the final rinse water as it enters the manifold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the glue traps in the dish area with two dead adult roaches and 2) a set of bowls (which are not used) wrapped in plastic underneath the prep sink with a small amount of liquid. This could possibly be a leak when the sprayer is used at this sink, but the sink itself was being used and there is no indication of an active leak as the cabinet itself is not wet. Clean these non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.comment:

750-1120e A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
